33-6.title: Do not buy a therapy or device that claims to cure paralysis, blindness or deafness
33-6.inPlainWords: No therapy or device has been proven to cure a complete spinal-cord injury, a mature cataract or a sensorineural hearing loss. A claim to 'cure' paralysis, blindness or deafness is a red flag. The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 and the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 give you a remedy, and the medical council can act on a false claim. Ask for the evidence, not a testimonial.
33-6.benefit: The RPwD Act, 2016 protects the rights of a person with a disability and prohibits discrimination. The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 covers a misleading advertisement and a deficient service. The National Medical Commission and the state medical council can act on a false claim by a doctor. A device needs a CDSCO registration where it is a medical device. A 'miracle cure' that delays a proven treatment can cause harm.
33-6.cost: No cost to ask for the evidence. A second opinion from a government hospital is cheap.
33-6.caveats: Rehabilitation, physiotherapy and assistive devices can improve function; they are not a cure. A claim based only on testimonials is not evidence. Do not stop a proven treatment for a miracle cure.
33-6.sources: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Consumer Protection Act, 2019. <https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/>; National Medical Commission. <https://www.nmc.org.in/>; Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation. <https://cdsco.gov.in/>

33-10.title: Mention your disability certificate in a job application: it can bring a reservation, a concession or a support
33-10.inPlainWords: A disability certificate and a UDID can make you eligible for a reservation in a government post, a fee concession, a scholarship and a workplace accommodation. Mention it at the application stage, not only at the interview, and keep a copy of the certificate. A private employer may also get a benefit for employing a person with a disability. You do not have to disclose a disability that does not affect the job, but a support or a reservation usually needs the certificate.
33-10.benefit: The RPwD Act, 2016 provides a 4% reservation in government establishments for the identified disabilities and requires an equal-opportunity policy. The UDID card is the single document for the benefits. A private employer can claim a deduction under the Income-tax Act for employing a person with a disability. The Act prohibits discrimination in promotion and pay. A reasonable accommodation can include a ramp, a screen reader or flexible hours.
33-10.cost: The certificate is free or low cost. A private employer's support varies.
33-10.caveats: A reservation applies to an identified post and a government establishment. A private employer is not bound by the 4% quota, but is bound by the anti-discrimination provisions. Keep the medical records for a reassessment.
33-10.sources: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities. <https://depwd.gov.in/>; Income-tax Department. <https://www.incometax.gov.in/>

33-20.title: If you are denied a job, a promotion or equal pay because of a disability, the RPwD Act gives you a remedy
33-20.inPlainWords: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 prohibits discrimination in employment, promotion and pay, and requires a reasonable accommodation. A government establishment must follow the reservation and the equal-opportunity policy. A private employer must not discriminate. You can complain to the state commissioner for persons with disabilities, the labour authority or a court. Keep the advertisement, the emails and the pay records.
33-20.benefit: Sections 20 and 21 of the RPwD Act, 2016 prohibit discrimination and require an equal-opportunity policy. The state commissioner can inquire into a complaint and recommend action. The labour court or the civil court can award compensation. The Act also provides for a grievance redressal officer in a government establishment. A union or an NGO can help with the complaint.
33-20.cost: No cost to complain to the commissioner. A lawyer's fee for a court case; legal aid is available.
33-20.caveats: A 'disability' must fall within the Act's list and be certified. A delay can weaken the case. A settlement should be in writing.
33-20.sources: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities. <https://depwd.gov.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
